title: Complete pro-etale compact-support base change
statement:
Let $(A,I)$ satisfy [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum], with $P_n=A/I^n$, and use its completed coefficient sheaves $A_T=\varprojlim_n(P_n)_T$ and categories $D(T_{\mathrm{proet}},A)=D(\operatorname{Mod}(A_T))$. Let
$$\begin{array}{ccc}X'&\xrightarrow{g'}&X\\
f'\downarrow&&\downarrow f\\
Y'&\xrightarrow{g}&Y\end{array}$$
be a cartesian compact-support square [def-cbc-compact-support-square], with $f$ separated of finite type and $g$ arbitrary. Supply a compactification $c=(j:X\hookrightarrow\overline X,p:\overline X\to Y)$ with $j$ quasi-compact open and $p$ proper [def-weil-pbc-projection-compactification], and its base change $c'=(j',p')$, with $\bar g:\overline X'\to\overline X$. Extension by zero for the completed sheaf $A_{\overline X}$ means the exact localized ringed-site functor of [lem-pur-site-restriction-module-adjunction-exact]; restriction of $A_{\overline X}$ to $X$ is $A_X$. Put $Rf_!^c=Rp_*j_!$ and $Rf'_!^{c'}=Rp'_*j'_!$.
Let $K\in D(X_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$ be derived $I$-complete [def-weil-pbc-intrinsic-completion], and equip its reductions $K_n$ with compatible witnesses $\alpha_n:\nu_X^*L_n\xrightarrow{\sim}K_n$, $L_n\in D^+(X_{\mathrm{et}},P_n)$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-origin-witness]. Then the completed compact-support exchange intended by [def-cbc-completed-exchange-map], explicitly the ordered composite
$$\begin{aligned}
\operatorname{Ex}^{\mathrm{comp},c}_!(K):Lg^*_{\mathrm{comp}}Rp_*j_!K
&\xrightarrow{\operatorname{Ex}^{\mathrm{comp}}_{p,j_!K}}Rp'_*L\bar g^*_{\mathrm{comp}}j_!K\\
&\xrightarrow{Rp'_*(\beta_{j,K})}Rp'_*j'_!Lg'^*_{\mathrm{comp}}K,
\end{aligned}$$
where $Lg^*_{\mathrm{comp}}$ is [def-weil-pbc-completed-pullback] and $\beta$ is the canonical comparison intended by [lem-cbc-completed-extension-zero-comparison], is an isomorphism. Specify the open comparison by the ordered maps
$$L\bar g^*_{\mathrm{comp}}j_!K\cong\operatorname{Rlim}(G_{\bar g}j_!K_\bullet)\xrightarrow{\operatorname{Rlim}(\beta_\bullet)}\operatorname{Rlim}(j'_!G_{g'}K_\bullet)\cong j'_!Lg'^*_{\mathrm{comp}}K,$$
using the canonical finite-reduction and extension/derived-limit comparisons and the open unit-mate $\beta_\bullet$ of [lem-cbc-strict-tower-proper-open-calculus], after restriction to constant $A$ coefficients as in [lem-weil-pbc-constant-completion-equivalence]. The last arrow is the inverse of the canonical $j'_!$ derived-limit comparison. It is natural in $K$, agrees under the canonical compactification comparisons, is the identity for identity base changes, and satisfies horizontal and vertical pasting after inserting the canonical composition identifications. For vertical pasting, compactifications of both morphisms and their composite are supplied, as in [thm-cbc-finite-torsion]. Thus it defines the asserted compactification-independent exchange $Lg^*_{\mathrm{comp}}Rf_!K\xrightarrow{\sim}Rf'_!Lg'^*_{\mathrm{comp}}K$.

proof.text: Restriction evaluates on the open slice, hence $A_T|_W=\lim_n(P_n)_W=A_W$. Exact ringed extension has the invertible derived open unit by the open-tensor normalization; transport through the slice equivalence gives the published open adjunction unit, independently of its presentation. The completed restriction/direct-image scalar equation is checked after every finite projection. Each finite equation follows from constant sheafification and the site counit. The limit projections are jointly monic, so the completed scalar equation follows. The site adjunction then lifts to module restriction and direct image; its unit evaluates on the open projection. This is the uniquely section-normalized unit, and its transpose is the unique-left-adjoint isomorphism. For Cartesian open base change, the transpose defining beta inverse is invertible because the open unit and square compositor are. Ordinary open base change identifies its target with an object in the essential image of the fully faithful open extension, so the counit there is invertible as well. For a clopen immersion, the normalized completed restriction scalar map is the composite of the inverse coefficient identification and the canonical site-adjunction comparison, hence invertible. Transport the existing reverse module adjunction across this scalar equivalence. Uniqueness of left adjoints identifies its extension with the published extension by zero. Exact localization and the pull-to-restriction isomorphism give a reverse derived adjunction. Uniqueness of right adjoints identifies extension by zero with direct image. Full faithfulness makes the pull/direct-image unit invertible on the extension image, and the specified open-to-direct-image map is a composite of this unit and the inverse open unit, hence invertible.

proof.text: Apply the independent-origin proper theorem to $p,j_!K$. Compose its isomorphism with $Rp\prime_*(\beta)$ from completed open comparison. The open-mate identification gives $r(\beta^{\mathrm{comp}}_K)=\lambda_{j\prime}^{-1}L(\beta_\bullet)$, so the specified ordered $R\lim(\beta_\bullet)$ formula is this invertible comparison; its factors are invertible by the strict open calculus and Step 2. Completed-pullback reduction gives the complete target. The inverse is the reverse composite of the two inverses. The Koszul/quotient comparison identifies the completeness unit used here.

proof.text: For identity base change, use the normalized proper identity equation from [lemma-weil-pbc-completed-exchange-coherence]. The ordinary open identity [lem-cbc-ordinary-open-exchange-identity], the completion-unit equation for the completed open exchange, and the reflection property [lem-weil-pbc-completed-pullback-reflection] give the completed open identity. Completeness of the input follows from Koszul/quotient comparison; completeness of its open extension follows from completed open comparison; proper direct image preserves it. The finite-origin theorem supplies the witnesses needed for the proper identity equation. Substitute both identities into the two-factor exchange and cancel the adjacent completed identity isomorphisms under proper pushforward. For the remaining horizontal pasting law, the strict horizontal theorem and functorial Rlim with Step 4 remain the planned route. Naturality against an arbitrary second input follows from ambient proper naturality and naturality of the completed open comparison.

proof.text: Refinement invertibility and base-change interchange still use the strict refinement-coherence route and its Rlim realization. For the compactifications clause, prove naturality directly: the defining component is a composite of whiskered natural transformations, hence its naturality square commutes. Use [lem-cbc-completed-refinement-map-functoriality] for the unit and composition laws of the actual cbcRefinementMap. For two common refinements, cofilteredness [lem-cbc-compactifiable-cofiltered] gives a cospan equalizing their first arrows; a further equalizer equalizes their second arrows. Applying the contravariant composition law to the two legs of that further common refinement inserts the same invertible factor on each side of a comparison; inverse-composite cancellation removes it. Thus the comparison is independent of both the common refinement and its arrows. For a fixed common refinement, the cocycle law follows by cancellation of the middle comparison isomorphism. All these categorical assembly and cancellation steps are proved in Lean, using the separately stated cbcRefinementMap_isIso for invertibility. The actual refinement composite is stored as the natural transformation [def-cbc-completed-refinement-transformation], whose component is cbcRefinementMap; its structural naturality field supplies the first clause without unfolding derived-functor data.

blueprint_update.statement:
Work in the setting of [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting]. Let $E/\Ql$ be a finite
extension with ring of integers $\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\pi_E$, regard
$\mathcal O_E$ as the condensed ring $\underline{\mathcal O}_E$
([det-def-sfb-condensed-ring]), and put $\mathcal O_{E,X}=p_X^*\mathcal O_E$
([det-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients]). Let

$$
\begin{array}{ccc}
X'&\xrightarrow{g'}&X\\
f'\downarrow&&\downarrow f\\
Y'&\xrightarrow{g}&Y
\end{array}
$$

be a cartesian square of the setting, let $c$ be a compactification of $f$ and
$c'$ its base change. Then the compact-support base change morphism of
[sk-def-sfb-shriek-base-change-morphism]

$$
\Ex^c_!(K):Lg^*Rf^c_!K\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }Rf'^{\,c'}_!Lg'^*K
$$

is an isomorphism for every $K\in\Dbc(X,\mathcal O_E)$, natural in $K$; here
$Rf^c_!=Rp_*\circ i_!$ is the lower shriek of [sk-def-sfb-dc-lower-shriek]
on the condensed categories $\Dbc(-,\mathcal O_E)$. For proper $f$ and
$c=(\mathrm{id},f)$ it is the proper base change isomorphism
$Lg^*Rf_*K\cong Rf'_*Lg'^*K$.

No completed pullback enters: $Lg^*$ and $Lg'^*$ preserve
$\Dbc(-,\mathcal O_E)$, whose objects are derived $\pi_E$-complete
$\mathcal O_{E,X}$-complexes ([def-pe-derived-complete],
[sk-prop-integral-criterion]), so the ordinary pullback of a constructible
integral complex is already complete.

proof.text:
Write $c=(X\xrightarrow{i}Z\xrightarrow{p}Y)$, $c'=(X'\xrightarrow{i'}Z'\xrightarrow{p'}Y')$ and
$\bar g:Z'\to Z$ for the projection. By
[sk-def-sfb-shriek-base-change-morphism], $\Ex^c_!(K)$ is the composite

$$
Lg^*Rp_*i_!K\xrightarrow{\ \mathrm{BC}\ }Rp'_*L\bar g^*i_!K
\xrightarrow{\ (\Ex^{j})^{-1}\ }Rp'_*i'_!Lg'^*K .
$$

The object $i_!K$ lies in $\Dbc(Z,\mathcal O_E)$
([sk-def-sfb-dc-restricted-functors]). The first arrow is the proper base
change map for the cartesian square formed by $p$ and $g$, evaluated on
$i_!K$; it is an isomorphism by [sk-thm-sfb-proper-base-change] with
$\Lambda=\mathcal O_E$, since $\Dctf=\Dbc$ at this coefficient ring
([sk-thm-existence]). The second arrow is $Rp'_*$ applied to the inverse of
the extension-by-zero base change isomorphism of
[sk-def-sfb-open-base-change] for the cartesian open square formed by $i$ and
$\bar g$. Hence $\Ex^c_!(K)$ is an isomorphism. Both arrows are natural
transformations, so the composite is natural in $K$. For proper $f$ and
$c=(\mathrm{id},f)$ the second arrow is the identity and $\Ex^c_!$ is the
proper base change map.
